**CYPRUS CROWNED: American Model Frances Marie Burke Takes Top Honors at Prestigious Miss Cyprus Pageant**

Nicosia, Cyprus - In a stunning upset, American model Frances Marie Burke was crowned the winner of the coveted Miss Cyprus beauty contest, held at the luxurious Four Seasons Hotel in Nicosia on Saturday evening. The 25-year-old stunner from New York City edged out 19 other contestants from around the world to claim the coveted title, impressing judges with her poise, elegance, and captivating stage presence. "I'm completely overwhelmed and humbled by this incredible honor," Burke said in an exclusive interview with our publication, beaming with pride. "Competing against such talented and beautiful women was an experience I'll never forget, and to be chosen as the winner is truly a dream come true." Burke, who has modeled for top designers and appeared on the covers of numerous fashion magazines, wowed the judges with her stunning looks, impeccable style, and impressive answers to the panel's questions. "Frances was a standout from the very beginning," said Maria Georgiou, a member of the judging panel and renowned fashion designer. "Her confidence, charisma, and natural beauty shone through in every aspect of the competition. She truly embodies the spirit of Miss Cyprus." The competition, now in its 20th year, attracted a record number of applicants from around the globe. The contestants were put through a rigorous series of challenges, including a swimsuit round, evening gown segment, and a question-and-answer session. According to pageant organizers, this year's event saw a significant increase in viewership, with over 1 million people tuning in to watch the live broadcast. "Frances's win is a testament to the growing global appeal of the Miss Cyprus pageant," said Andreas Christodoulou, president of the Miss Cyprus Organization. "We're thrilled to have her as our new ambassador, and we're confident she'll do an outstanding job representing Cyprus on the international stage." As the new Miss Cyprus, Burke will embark on a year-long reign, during which she will participate in various charity events, fashion shows, and promotional activities. She will also represent Cyprus at the upcoming Miss World pageant in December. When asked about her plans for her reign, Burke said, "I'm excited to use my platform to make a positive impact on the lives of others.

Reply with JSON only, in this form:
{"relevant": true, "cards": [{"entity": "", "sense": "", "answer": "", "as_of": "", "claim_kind": "", "attributed_to": "", "evidence": "", "claim": ""}]}

"relevant": false if the document is about some other topic and is of no use for the question; then "cards" is [].
"cards": one card for each answer the document itself gives to the question. Usually that is one card. It is several cards if the document gives several answers, such as a list of names: one card each. It is [] if the document gives no answer. The question may fit several things that share a name: whichever of them this document is about, report its answer. If the document only says that some answer is wrong, write no card for that answer.

The fields of a card:
- "entity": who or what this answer is about, as specifically as the document identifies it: the full name, plus the details the document gives that tell it apart from others with the same name (what kind of thing it is, profession or role, nationality or place, years, creator, other names), even where the question does not ask about them. At most about 25 words.
- "sense": which event, edition, version, condition, place or measure the answer refers to, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "answer": the answer, copied from the document as it is written there, and short: a full name, a date, a number with its unit, or a short phrase. For a yes-or-no question, "yes" or "no".
- "as_of": the date at which this was true, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "claim_kind": "factual", or "opinion" for a judgment, a recommendation or a contested finding.
- "attributed_to": who or what the document says this comes from, such as a census, a study or a named person, if it says; otherwise "not stated".
- "evidence": the sentence of the document that gives the answer, copied word for word. Two sentences if one is not enough.
- "claim": one sentence that states the answer on its own and names the entity.

Inside a JSON string, write a double quote as \".
